topic: The 1929 Wall Street Crash: How panic selling sealed the Great Depression

script.title: 1929 Wall Street Crash: How Panic Selling Fueled the Great Depression
script.hook: What if the crash never happened?

scenes.text: What if the crash never happened?

motion_action.headline: What if the crash never happened?

scenes.text: The Dow fell from about three hundred to sixty nine points.
Investors rushed to sell stocks, flooding the market with massive volume.
Bank runs froze credit across the nation.

motion_action.statement: Bank runs froze credit across the nation

scenes.text: Industrial output fell by about a quarter within a year.
Unemployment jumped from under five percent in 1929 to about twenty‑five percent by 1933.
Panic = Depression. Selling amplified the slump.
Why did fear spread so fast? Psychology of herd behavior triggered mass sell‑offs.

motion_action.result_headline: Psychology of herd behavior triggered mass sell‑offs

scenes.text: 1929 panic sell vs 2020 COVID sell shows similar fallout.
Now you know why panic sells doom economies:

motion_action.headline: Now you know why panic sells doom

script.description:
The 1929 Wall Street Crash showed how panic selling can turn a recession into a depression. Learn the mechanics behind the crash and its lasting impact. Discover why herd behavior still matters today.

#Shorts #money #economics #finance
script.comment_question: Which panic moment in history scares you the most?
sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics unemployment records
review_notes: FIXED: Scene 3: "Investors dumped stocks at a rate of roughly three million shares per day." (No evidence supports that exact daily share volume during the crash.)
FIXED: Scene 6: "Unemployment rose to ten percent, then to twenty five percent by nineteen thirty three." (Historical unemployment was ~4.7% in 1929 and ~25% in 1933, not 10% in 1929.)
